# Real-Time Sync

## Decision rule

Opt in only when both are true:

1. The data can change without the current user acting.
2. The user needs to see that change before refreshing or navigating.

A local agent edit does not meet this rule. The chat run stream already
invalidates action queries and source counters after each side-effecting tool
and again at run end, without opening a background poll.

### Opt in

- **Slides deck editor:** another collaborator can edit the open deck.
- **Mail inbox:** new mail can arrive while the inbox is open.
- **A watched job:** a background job changes progress while the user watches it.
- **Cross-tab state:** state must converge across this user's open tabs without a
  new action.

### Keep it off

- Public, anonymous, marketing, docs, and SSR pages.
- Settings, forms, and read-mostly lists or dashboards. Refresh them on focus or
  navigation instead.
- Single-user agent edits. The chat run stream handles those.
- Pages where an update is useful eventually but not before the next refresh.

## Cost and behavior

`useDbSync()` has no background transport unless the page opts in with a
non-empty reason. One transport is shared per tab. A visible opted-in tab polls
at 1 minute, then 2, then 5 minutes while idle; user activity or a local
mutation resets that sequence. Hidden tabs pause by default. During an active
agent run, opted-in sync can poll at its configured `interval`; local tool
completion and run-end invalidation do not depend on that poll.

On a long-lived host, same-process changes stream over
`/_agent-native/events`; polling is the cross-process fallback. On a production
serverless host, the local events endpoint refuses the long-lived stream and
`/_agent-native/poll` carries remote changes. The paid Hosted Realtime Sync
Gateway is not required for this pattern.

While a collab doc shows another person present, the transport polls every
2.5 s instead (`acquireCollabPollBoost()`, held by the collab client, not by
pages). It is a no-op whenever a stream is connected, lapses after 3 minutes
without input or remote events, and never applies to lone tabs.

## Use the hook

Declare the reason beside the route gate so reviewers can see why the page pays
for remote sync:

```tsx
useDbSync({
  queryClient,
  realtime: isPrivateDeckEditorPath(location.pathname)
    ? { reason: "other collaborators can edit this deck while it is open" }
    : undefined,
  pauseWhenHidden: true,
});
```

The reason is required by the TypeScript API. Opt in only for a named private
or authenticated route; public, documentation, and SSR pages should not start a
background transport.

An opted-in page only hears about an action when its change event reaches the
current user. By default an `action` event reaches the actor alone, so a
collaborator's comment, save, or agent edit never arrives. Declare
`changeResource: (input, result) => ({ resourceType, resourceId })` on the
mutating action and the event also reaches everyone who can read that resource.
Name it from `input` when the call carries the resource id (Content's
`documentChangeResource`, Slides' comment actions) and from `result` when the
call is keyed by a child id (Design's `designChangeResource` for
`delete-file`); return `null` for a call that changed nothing. Do not publish a
parallel per-template event for the same purpose.

Do not start `subscribeSyncEvents()` or an `EventSource` in a feature to bypass
the decision. `subscribeSyncEvents()` is a lower-level transport subscription
used by the existing Yjs collaboration client and narrow framework plumbing.
Keep Yjs collaborative editing on its existing channel.

## Query freshness

Prefer `useActionQuery()` for action-backed data. Mutating actions refresh local
action observers; the chat run stream also invalidates them for agent tool
side effects. Raw queries should include the relevant source counters:

```tsx
const versions = useChangeVersions(["dashboards", "action"]);
useQuery({
  queryKey: ["dashboard", id, versions],
  queryFn: () => fetchDashboard(id),
  placeholderData: (previous) => previous,
});
```

That covers local chat-run edits. Remote edits reach the counter through
`useDbSync()` only on an opted-in page. Use `useReconciledState` when a form or
inline editor copies a query value into local state so incoming data does not
replace active typing.

URL commands (`__set_url__`, `set-url`, and `set-search-params`) and
`refresh-screen` also flow through local chat events. The sidebar listens for
screen refresh only while its panel is open or a chat run is active; public docs
can disable that boundary with `screenRefreshEnabled={false}`.

## Source counters

On local tool completion, `useDbSync()` advances the action counter and any
other raw-query source counters currently observed by the page. Generic tool
completion events do not identify their data domain, so keep raw-query source
lists narrow. Remote sync events advance their specific source counters.

| Source | Changed by |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | A successful mutating action or local chat-run side-effect completion |
| `app-state` | Writes to `application_state`, including URL commands |
| `settings` | Writes to `settings` |
| `dashboards`, `analyses`, `extensions` | Domain-specific mutations that emit those sources |
| `collab` | Yjs collaborative document updates |
| `screen-refresh` | The explicit `refresh-screen` agent tool |

Use `useChangeVersions()` when one query depends on more than one source.

## Avoid

- Do not create manual polling loops or a second `EventSource`.
- Do not enable background sync for a whole app root when only one private
  route needs remote updates.
- Do not assume a successful local action is a reason for a background
  subscriber; use local mutation invalidation and the chat run stream.
- Do not blanket-invalidate template queries when a source-versioned query or
  action-backed query can target the refreshed data.

name: recurring-jobs
content:
---
name: recurring-jobs
description: >-
  The legacy manage-jobs compatibility surface, job files under jobs/, and cron
  scheduler internals. Use when maintaining manage-jobs integrations or
  debugging the scheduler.
metadata:
  internal: true
---

# Recurring Jobs (Compatibility)

## Rule

Recurring Jobs is the legacy name and API for scheduled automations. Jobs live
as resource files under `jobs/` with YAML frontmatter for scheduling metadata.

Read `automations` for the product model, trigger types, frontmatter fields,
organization scope, and when to prefer `manage-automations` over `manage-jobs`.
This skill covers only what is specific to the legacy scheduled path: the
`manage-jobs` tool and the cron scheduler behind it.

## How It Works

1. User asks for something recurring via the agent chat
2. Agent uses `manage-jobs` tool (action: "create") to write a job file at `jobs/<name>.md`
3. A scheduler tick finds due jobs about once a minute. Long-running servers
   fire it in-process; Netlify, Vercel, and Cloudflare fire it from a platform
   trigger the build emits; AWS Lambda has no trigger, so jobs never fire there
4. Due jobs enter the shared background-automation runner, on the same
   execution lifecycle as event automations
5. Job results are saved as chat threads

## Connected MCPs in background jobs

When a job needs a connected remote MCP, bind the exact advertised
`mcp__<server>__<tool>` names through `mcpTools`. The scheduler passes that
definition to the shared runner, which resolves only that allowlist under the
persisted creator/org request context and never stores or exposes OAuth tokens,
URLs, or arbitrary proxy targets.

Use an app-owned bounded import/upsert action for writes. Keep provider-specific
response mapping, provenance, deduplication, and write policy in the app rather
than in core. For example, a job can read meeting notes from any connected MCP
and pass normalized action items to an app's idempotent `import` action.

## Job Tool (built in)

| Tool          | Action     | Purpose                                                    |
| ------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manage-jobs` | `create`   | Create a recurring job (name, cron schedule, instructions); fails if the name exists |
| `manage-jobs` | `list`     | List all jobs and their status                             |
| `manage-jobs` | `update`   | Update schedule, instructions, or toggle enabled           |

## Job files an app owns

`create` never replaces an existing job file, so a name that collides with an
app's file (Factory's `factories/<id>/<name>`) is refused instead of reset.
An app that stores its own settings in a job's frontmatter marks the file with
`triggerType`, which makes `list`, `update`, and `delete` skip it and sends the
caller to `manage-automations`. Edit those files only through the owning app's
actions, and patch fields in place; rebuilding a file from the fields the writer
knows drops the rest while the job keeps running.

Any write to a `jobs/` file that removes a frontmatter field other than run
bookkeeping is recorded as a `job-fields-dropped` audit event (org admins read
it with `list-audit-events` and `action: "job-fields-dropped"`). Its input names
the writer, the dropped fields, and the agent thread and run that made it.

## UI Surface

`/agent#jobs` is the stable compatibility URL for the Agent page's
**Automations** tab, which lists legacy scheduled jobs alongside trigger-aware
automations and is backed by the scoped list/manage actions. Direct users there
instead of describing job files when they just want to view or toggle scheduled
work.

## Key Files

| File                                  | Purpose                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/core/src/jobs/cron.ts`      | Cron parsing (`nextOccurrence`, `isValidCron`, `describeCron`) |
| `packages/core/src/jobs/scheduler.ts` | Job execution engine (`processRecurringJobs`)            |
| `packages/core/src/jobs/tools.ts`     | Agent tool (`manage-jobs` with create/list/update actions) |
| `packages/core/src/client/agent-page/` | `AgentJobsTab`, the `/agent#jobs` surface                |

## Related Skills

- `automations` — The primary Scheduled/Event product model
- `actions` — How tools and actions work
- `delegate-to-agent` — How jobs invoke the agent loop

name: refactor-plan
content:
---
name: refactor-plan
description: >-
  Judge whether a system is fragile or just fast-moving, and write a
  ticket-ready refactor plan for one root problem, with measured evidence and
  a stable fingerprint. Use after system history (or a bug trace) points at a
  systemic problem worth fixing at the root.
scope: dev
metadata:
  internal: true
---

# Refactor plan

## Judge first

`references/rubric.md` separates fragile from fast-moving from coupled, and
sets confidence. The counts from system-history are leads. A plan needs
a named repeated mechanism, taken from diffs you read.

## Scaffold

```bash
pnpm exec tsx .agents/skills/refactor-plan/scripts/new-plan.ts --run <id> \
  --slug <kebab> --title "<imperative line>" --systems a,b \
  --area <Framework|Slides|Design|Clips|Content|Dispatch|General> [--force]
```

It reads the run's `analysis.json`. Every system must be one analyze
scored. When the run has a `bug.json`, the plan becomes a bug plan:

- it adds a Trigger section, and quotes the report when it has no link;
- its paths are the focus files only;
- its frontmatter gets `trigger: bug` and the report as `source`.

Plans go to `<plansDir>/<run>/<slug>.md` (see `config.json`).

## Fill it

Replace every `TODO(agent)` marker, `summary`, and `confidence`, following
`references/plan-guide.md`. Keep slugs stable across runs. The
fingerprint comes from the systems and the slug, and ticket dedup keys on it.

A plan is finished when fragility-common's `findings-upsert.ts` accepts
it.

name: reliable-mutations
content:
---
name: reliable-mutations
description: >-
  How the agent must perform writes so they actually persist under the hosted
  foreground run budget and long-running background handoffs. Use whenever you
  create, update, delete, or batch-write app data — especially "do this for many
  items" loops, or any task where the user expects N things to end up saved.
scope: dev
---

# Reliable Mutations

## Rule

Make a change in **one atomic call** when the action supports it, then **verify
the persisted end state and report concrete proof** (counts/ids). Never drive a
multi-step change by looping many small writes, and never report success from a
tool ✓ alone.

## Why

Hosted foreground agent runs have a short soft budget so they can hand off
cleanly under synchronous serverless walls. Durable background runs get a much
longer budget, but they still should not rely on loops of many small writes:
continuations can retry the same intent and leave partial state if each item is
committed separately. One atomic call commits or fails as a unit; verification
turns a hopeful ✓ into a fact.

## How

1. **Prefer a single atomic call.** If an action accepts the whole set (add
   many, set all, bulk update), pass the full batch in one call so it commits
   atomically. Check the action surface for a batch/plural form before reaching
   for a loop.
2. **Do not loop many small writes under any run budget.** A sequence of N
   per-item writes can still leave partial or no state when a foreground run
   hands off, a background run continues, or an upstream provider fails. If no
   batch action exists, that is a gap in the action layer — add or extend an
   action that accepts the batch (see the `actions` skill) rather than papering
   over it with a loop.
3. **Verify the end state after writing.** Re-read the data (a list/read action,
   a count query) and confirm the result matches intent — the right number of
   rows, the expected ids/fields. Do this before you tell the user it worked,
   and include the relevant verification expectation in the app's `AGENTS.md`.
4. **Report proof-of-done, not vibes.** State concrete evidence: "saved 12 of 12
   panels (ids …)" or "updated 5 rows". Do not infer success from the presence
   of a tool ✓ on an individual call.
5. **On a time-budget cutoff, fail loud.** If the turn is cut before the change
   is fully committed and verified, say so explicitly and report what *did*
   persist (M of N) and what remains. Never round a partial or unverified write
   up to "done".

## Don't

- Don't loop `for each item: write(item)` for a large set in a single hosted
  turn.
- Don't claim completion because every tool call returned ✓ — a ✓ on an aborted
  chunk does not mean the row was committed.
- Don't silently shrink the scope ("I added a few of them") and present it as the
  finished task.
- Don't try to "fix" this by asking for a longer run timeout — the budget is
  correct; restructure the write instead.

## Related

- `actions` — define or extend a batch/atomic action when only per-item writes
  exist.
- `storing-data` — where app data lives and how reads/writes are scoped.
- `performance` — avoid query waterfalls when verifying end state.
- Design doc: `packages/core/docs/design/durable-agent-runs.md` — the real
  ceiling fix (checkpointed and durable runs); this skill is the agent-facing
  mitigation that reduces how often the ceiling is hit.

name: reporting-progress
content:
---
name: reporting-progress
description: >-
  What to say while long work is still running, and what a legal mid-task stop
  looks like. Use during any run over a few minutes — migrations, sweeps,
  babysit loops, automations, deploys — and at the moment you are tempted to
  stop and ask, report a blocker, or answer "how's it going?".
scope: dev
metadata:
  internal: true
---

# Reporting Progress

Measured on 2026-08-12, "had to chase status on a long-running run" was the
single most frequent correction in this repo — 86 in two weeks, more than
false-done and collisions combined. Every one of them is the user asking a
question the agent could have answered before being asked.

## A turn ends in exactly one of two shapes

**Done**, with the artifact that proves it — a command's output, a sha, a URL,
a screenshot file. `verifying-changes` says which artifact per area. A sentence
describing a check you would run is not an artifact.

**Blocked**, on one line:

```
BLOCKED: <what is stopping you> — unblock: <one thing the user can do in under a minute>
```

Anything else is a stall. "I'm looking into it", "let me know how you want to
proceed", and a status paragraph with no ask are all stalls.

## Exhaust this before writing BLOCKED

In the measured cases, every single "blocked" was a step the agent could have
taken:

1. Run it locally instead of waiting on a deploy or CI.
2. Drive the user's logged-in Chrome instead of asking them to click.
3. Read production directly — the DB URLs are in the template `.env` files.
4. Spawn a cheap subagent for the part you think you lack context for.
5. Pick the reversible option and say which one you picked.

A missing credential, a genuinely destructive action, and a decision only the
user can make are blockers. Nothing else on this list is.

## While it runs

Post a delta, not a heartbeat. "Tick 14, still running" is noise; the user
reads it as nothing happening — which, in the measured cases, it usually was.

- Every milestone, and at least every ~15 minutes: what changed since the last
  note, and the number that moved (rows copied, files swept, checks green).
- If the number has not moved in two consecutive notes, that is not a progress
  note — that is a stall. Say what is stuck and change the approach.
- If the user has to ask "still going?", that is a miss.

Never message another agent's thread to report your own progress, and never
tell peer threads to pause. Their work is not yours to stop.

name: review-latest-feedback
content:
---
name: review-latest-feedback
description: >-
  Sweep recent feedback (the Slack feedback channels, GitHub issues, CI on
  main, Sentry, Analytics errors, chat run health, deploys), fix as many real
  bugs as possible, ship them in one PR, then close the loop on every Slack
  report with 👀/✅/🎫 and one short plain-English reply. Use for scheduled or
  manual feedback sweeps, usually followed by /ship.
user-invocable: true
scope: dev
metadata:
  internal: true
---

# Review Latest Feedback

The job: find what's broken, fix as much of it as you can, ship it, and tell
each reporter in one friendly sentence what happened. A sweep is judged by
bugs fixed and merged, and by every claimed report getting a clear answer. It is
not judged by ledgers, receipts, or checker output.

## The contract

The detailed Slack reaction and reply rules are in
[slack-reaction-replies.md](references/slack-reaction-replies.md); read it before
marking, replying to, or closing any Slack report.

Slack reactions on a report's root message mean exactly this:

| Mark | Meaning                                   | When to add                                                                                      |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 👀   | "I'm on this"                             | Before you investigate, and only on reports you will finish answering in this run               |
| ✅   | "Fixed"                                   | After the fix is merged to `main` (main deploys to beta automatically)                           |
| 🎫   | "Needs a person"                          | A product call, access or credentials, info from the reporter, or a fix you couldn't land        |

A maintainer is a Builder.io team member in the workspace who is not the
reporter and not a bot. Maintainers steer the sweep with reactions on a root:

| A maintainer adds | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:mag:`           | Don't work on this; someone else will. Wins over everything below                        |
| `:yes-party:`     | Definitely do this, even if it looks ambiguous or like a UX change. Build the smallest version that does what was asked |
| `:upvote:`        | Same as `:yes-party:` for a feature request                                               |
| 👀 by hand        | They're working on it themselves; leave it (see "Open items first" for how to tell their 👀 from ours) |

Reactions can't be removed through the Slack connector, so never add one you
might need to take back. Every 👀 you add ends the run with a reply, plus
either ✅ or 🎫, or a fix PR that is still open and lists the report (its
merge adds the ✅).

Every claimed report gets **one** reply in its thread per outcome. The one exception is
the merged `✅` close-out after an in-review reply, which gets no second reply. Each reply must be:

- **An answer first:** if they asked something ("is this expected?"),
  answer it in the first words ("no, that's a bug"), not with a status.
- **Short:** one sentence, about 25 words at most, for someone who doesn't
  read code.
- **About what they'll notice:** say what changes for them ("recordings no
  longer get stuck on Saving"), not how it works ("cleanup now waits for the
  transcript"). Leave out file, function, and service names, PR numbers,
  ticket IDs, CI, logs, runs, "repro", "verified", "scope", "sweep", status
  labels ("In progress:", "Skipped:", "Resolved elsewhere:", "Blocked on
  human owner:", "Open - no question:"), and any mention of this workflow.
  Never report your own progress ("unreproduced", "not traced yet",
  "remains open"); say what happens next instead.
- **Clear on what happens next:** "I'll ..." when this workflow acts. When it
  needs a person, never name one and never say "the team", "product", "the
  framework team", "the owner", or "someone": say only what's known ("I
  couldn't reproduce this yet", "logged for a product decision"), add 🎫, and
  record it as needing a person with the reason. Never @-mention anyone.
- **Not a to-do list for them:** look things up yourself first (the
  message's time and author, their account and recent activity, logs, the
  linked page or screenshot). Ask only when nothing else can unblock it, and
  then ask one small thing, in this one reply. Never send a list of
  questions, never ask them to test, retry, re-record, pull, reinstall, or
  gather logs, and never come back later asking for something you could have
  asked the first time. If it needs access you don't have (credentials, admin
  rights, account changes), say it's logged for someone with access and add
  🎫; never hand it to the reporter.
- **Plain, not preachy:** don't explain how the product works unless they
  asked, don't tell them what they should do, and skip apologies, hedging,
  "actually", "just", "simply", and "Great catch!!".
- **True:** "fixed" only for a merged fix, and "on beta shortly" only after
  the merge. Before that, the fix is "in review". Never "fixed and verified"
  on the strength of a local check.
- **Once:** never post the same reply twice, and never follow up with one
  that adds nothing new.
- Link the PR on the word "fix" (`<url|fix>`), never by number.
- End with the bold line `**This was sent from a bot**` on its own line,
  once.

Don't reply at all to jokes, venting, banter, a message meant for a specific
teammate, or a thread a person is already handling. Once a person says they
have it, or asks the bot to stop, post nothing more in that thread. Before posting, reread the reply as the reporter: would they get it
in five seconds, know what happens next, and feel we did the legwork? Check
the draft before sending, not after: the first version is the one that
notifies them, so editing it afterwards doesn't undo it.

Good (each is the first line; the footer goes on the line below it):

- `thanks - the <https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/pull/1234|fix> so the export keeps your column order is merged and will be on beta shortly.`
- `thanks - once this <https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/pull/1234|fix> merges, the export will keep your column order; it's in review now.`
- `thanks - where that button should go is logged for a product decision.`
- `thanks - I couldn't find which deck this was; could you paste its link?`

So a full reply looks like:

```text
thanks - the <https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/pull/1234|fix> so the export keeps your column order is merged and will be on beta shortly.
**This was sent from a bot**
```

Real replies that missed, and what to send instead:

| Sent | Instead |
| --- | --- |
| "Could you send the recording link, approximate time, and browser so we can trace whether the clip produced media before it tried to save?" | Find the recording from the reporter and message time first. If you still can't: "thanks - I couldn't find which recording this was; could you paste its link?" |
| "cleanup now waits for the transcript, and a fix is ready. It should be on beta shortly." (sent before the merge) | "thanks - recordings will keep their transcript once this <url\|fix> is merged; it's in review now." |
| "I've left moving it somewhere easier to find for product to decide." | "thanks - where the editor should live is logged for a product decision." |
| "Partially fixed - PR #7512 merged the project-instructions/context carryover fix", after she'd asked whether FullStory could be added for the whole org | Answer that question first: "yes - I'll add it for everyone" or "not yet - that's logged for a decision". |
| "All fixed and verified. Please try again!" plus instructions to pull main and reinstall | "thanks - this <url\|fix> is merged and will be on beta shortly." No homework. |
| More replies after Shawn wrote "bot please stop! I've got this all fixed and in flight" | Nothing. A person has it. |
| "Thanks for correcting me, Julia - I misread the replies. ... Open - no question: I don't have enough source evidence to claim a fix." | Nothing: the thread was a joke. |
| Asked for the app URL, what was clicked, and the time; then, in a second reply, for the time zone. | One reply, one question, only for what you can't look up. The message's own timestamp already says when. |

## Boundaries

- **Slack:** only `#product-agent-native-feedback` (`C0ATH3CCZT4`)
  and `#qa-agent-native` (`C0C4U4XRT6X`), a narrower set the invocation
  names, or a caller's list (as in `factory-run`). Never
  react or reply elsewhere. Reply only in a report thread this workflow
  claimed with 👀 and investigated; a bot reply alone isn't a claim.
  Never start a new channel message.
- **Leave a report alone** when:
  - a maintainer put `:mag:` or their own 👀 on it (table above);
  - someone in the thread asked a specific person to look, a teammate says
    they're handling it, or a maintainer asked for a human on it;
  - another person's 👀 sits on it and they've been active in the last 3
    days;
  - an earlier run's PR for it is still open. That PR's `/ship` closes the
    report out when it merges.
- **PRs:** push to, comment on, or merge only the PR this run opened. PRs from
  other sessions share the active GitHub login (`gh api user --jq .login`), so
  authorship proves nothing: a PR under that login may be another thread's
  work in flight, and pushing to it lands unreviewed commits on it. Never touch any other PR unless the invocation names that exact PR and
  action. That holds inside `/ship` too: its "Your PRs" means this run's PR.
- **One run, one PR.** Every sweep PR is authored by the active GitHub login, so the
  author check can't tell runs apart: an
  open PR with a `Reports` section that this run didn't open belongs to
  another run that may still be working on it. Don't push to, reply on, or
  merge it; list it under "Still open from earlier runs".
- **Goals end with the run.** If you set a Codex goal, scope it to this run:
  name its PR once you have one, and end it after step 6 ("merge PR #N,
  close its Reports, append the recap"). Never set an open-ended goal such as
  "review feedback" or "fix my open PRs". Goals resume after restarts,
  so an open-ended one keeps running into the next scheduled sweep and
  collides with it.
- Use the connected Slack integration for every Slack read and write. Confirm
  which profile is connected before the first write; every reply and reaction
  posts as that profile.

## Dry run

On "dry run", run every step but send nothing:

- Record each reaction and the exact reply you'd post, linking the fix branch
  where the PR would go.
- Treat other runs' claims as unclaimed; honor a maintainer's `:mag:` and 👀.
- Publish one branch per fix group; skip PRs, merges, `/ship`, and comments.
- Skip the connected-profile check; use the state the invocation names.

<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
The factory VM runs this skill through `factory-run`, which differs on
purpose: replies post as the factory's own Slack app (no bot line, no profile
check), claims live in factory state, each fix group gets its own branch and
PR, and the watcher merges.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->

## 1. Collect (keep it under ~15 minutes)

Work in a task-owned worktree on fresh `origin/main`. If you start in a shared
checkout, or the expected worktree is missing, create one
(`git worktree add <path> origin/main`) and carry on. That is never a reason
to stop.

Window: roots posted in the last 5 days (or since the timestamp or permalink
the invocation gives), for new reports and open items alike. An older thread
is in the window too when we have already replied in it and a person has
replied since the window began: a channel read only shows roots, so search for
recent thread replies (`in:<#channel> is:thread after:<date>`) to find them.
Roots in `memory.md` under "Claimed reports", "Claimed, not yet answered",
or "Must handle next run" are always in the window. Other older threads are left as they are, except reports listed under
`Reports` in a sweep PR opened or merged in that window: those always get
their close-out.

Give each source below its own helper on the cheapest model (Luna in Codex,
Haiku in Claude Code), and close it as soon as it reports. A helper gathers;
you triage. The Slack helper returns every root a person posted in the window with no ✅, 🎫, or `:mag:`,
and every root with a person's reply newer than ours, one line each (link,
author, first line). It never filters, ranks, or drops one: a new report has
no reaction and no thread yet.

- **Read the channels.** Use `slack_read_channel` with
  `response_format: detailed` (paginate) back 5 days. Its output shows
  reaction counts but not who added them, so call `slack_get_reactions` on any
  root showing `eyes`, `white_check_mark`, `ticket`, `mag`, `yes-party`, or
  `upvote`. Avoid `hasmy:`; run the
  [backstop](references/slack-reaction-replies.md#backstop-for-unclaimed-roots).
- **Open items first.** Verify the connected profile's 👀 on the root and workflow ownership
  from a matching run recap, proof-bearing PR, or automation memory claim.
  A bot reply, reaction, or memory entry alone is insufficient. Investigate
  before replying, and read the thread for human updates. A root
  listed in the `Reports` section of a sweep
  PR that is still open and that this run didn't open belongs to the run
  working on that PR: don't react
  or reply there, and leave it out of your self-check; just list it under
  "Still open from earlier runs". If that PR has had no push in 24 hours,
  its run has stopped: its reports are yours again. Of the remaining
  workflow roots, those without ✅ or 🎫 come first in this run. A newer
  human reply is context, not by itself a reason to respond: investigate the
  claimed report and leave conversations already handled by people alone. A
  root with 🎫 and our reply after its latest human message is already answered: you may still fix it, but post nothing there
  until the fix merges. A
  reply like "still broken" after a ✅ means the earlier fix failed. Find what
  that fix changed and why it didn't hold before trying again.
- **New reports:** roots from the last 5 days. React and reply on the root
  message's own `ts`. A channel-history row whose `thread_ts` differs from its
  `ts` is a reply that was also sent to the channel: use its `thread_ts`
  parent instead. Read the thread for every root
  that looks like a report. Open screenshots and attachments, since the error
  text in a screenshot is often the whole diagnosis.
- **Other sources.** Unread or failing sources are reported as
  **unavailable**, never as "nothing found".
  - GitHub: open issues updated in the window
    (`gh issue list --state open --search "updated:>=<date>"`). Skip ones
    someone else has offered to fix.
  - Sentry (through its connector, or the local reader the invocation
    names) and Agent-Native Analytics (`list-error-issues`, then
    `get-error-issue`): unresolved, recent, and repo-owned. Rank by users
    affected. An error with a stack trace is already a reproduction lead.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
  - CI on main: `pnpm ci:red-report` (exit 2 means CI unavailable, not
    clean).
  - Chat run health: `node scripts/chat-health.mjs --hours 72`; see
    [chat-run-health.md](references/chat-run-health.md) for what each failure
    reason usually means.
  - Deploys and releases: `gh run list --branch main --status failure --limit 30`
    for the deploy, release, desktop, and publish workflows.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->

## 2. Triage: lean toward fixing

Put each report in one bucket:

- **Fix:** anything objectively broken. This means errors, nothing happening
  on click, lost or wrong data, regressions, slowness, jank, and visible
  defects like clipped or overlapping text, unreadable contrast, or a broken
  layout. A credible "nothing happens" counts as evidence.
- **Build:** a feature request or UX change carrying a maintainer's
  `:upvote:` or `:yes-party:`.
- **Needs a person (🎫):** subjective product or UX changes no maintainer has
  endorsed (add, move, hide, or restyle controls; "hard to find"), work that needs access or settings only
  a person has, a provider outage, or a report you can't act on without one
  missing fact. A bug you couldn't reproduce by reading code is still a Fix.
- **Not actionable:** praise, chatter, announcements, things a human already
  answered, duplicates of something already in this run. These get no
  reaction and no reply.

Issues from the error and health sources above go in the same buckets,
ranked with the Slack reports by people affected. They have no thread to react on,
so they appear only in the recap.

Claim Fix reports in order of people affected. Unfinished claims stay in
"Claimed reports" for the next run. Any Fix, Build, or Needs-a-person root you leave
unclaimed gets no reaction, only one line in the recap saying why, so
nothing is dropped silently. That covers every candidate your source helpers
return: each one ends the run either claimed or on a recap line with its
reason.

In scheduled and manual runs, record each root (channel and ts) under "Claimed
reports" in the feedback automation's `memory.md`, then add and verify 👀
before investigating. A record alone does not establish a claim: the root
must also have the verified 👀 from this workflow. Retain the record until
the report is resolved or a person takes over. If shared memory is unavailable,
do not claim new roots.

## 3. Fix as many as you can

- Group related reports so one cause gets one fix. Give each independent
  group a fresh subagent on your own model and effort, with disjoint files,
  or fix it in the main thread. Never hand a finished helper a new job; start
  a fresh one. The main thread plans, reviews diffs, and integrates.
- **Reproduce before you edit.** Get the failure on screen first: a test
  that fails, the action returning the wrong thing, a stack trace, or the
  flow broken in a signed-in local app. Reading code is not an attempt:
  write the report's steps as a failing test, or walk them in the signed-in
  app. A broken setup isn't an attempt either: when a test can't load or an
  install fails, fix the setup (install what's missing, or free space by
  removing only this run's own build output) or
  walk the steps in the signed-in app instead. Only after a real attempt fails does a report become 🎫, and its
  recap line says what you ran. No reproduction means no code change.
- **Check the history.** `git log --since=30.days --oneline -- <files>`: if
  this surface was fixed before for the same symptom, that fix treated a
  symptom. Find the shared cause (`fix-at-the-boundary`) instead of adding
  one more patch, and look for the same pattern elsewhere.
- **Prove it.** The check has to fail with the fix's source changes put
  back to `main` and pass with them. A check that passes without your fix
  doesn't test the bug: write one that does. Tests that read source text
  never count. For a purely visual fix, before and after screenshots are
  evidence, not automated proof: before merging, a human must open both and
  confirm they show the reported change. Put the evidence under the report in
  the PR's `Reports` section. A test-only change (test files, optional
  `.changeset/`) needs only `fix-proof: test-only`.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
  Commit the fix and its check, then run
  `node scripts/fix-proof.ts --fix <that commit> -- <the check>` from the
  repo root and paste its `fix-proof: proven ...` line, unchanged, under
  each report it fixes (`visual: <before> <after>` for a purely visual
  fix). The required `Lint & format` check runs this gate for PRs with a
  `Reports` section and re-runs machine proofs. It marks visual-only reports
  as needing human validation before merge. The second
  opinion below reads the red output to confirm the check failed on the
  bug, not on setup.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->
- **Two misses, then stop guessing.** If two attempts don't turn the check
  green, stop editing and capture the real failure first (stack, logs, the
  reporter's actual data). If that doesn't settle it within about 30
  minutes, it becomes 🎫 with one line on what you learned.
- **Second opinion before the PR, every time.** Give a fresh subagent on
  your own model only the report text, the diff, and the proof, and ask: does
  the check exercise what the reporter saw, is this the cause or a symptom,
  and what edge case breaks it? Fix what it finds before you open the PR.
- **Keep fixes small.** Each report's fix goes in its own commit so a bad
  one can be reverted alone. A fix that grows past about 300 lines, or into
  a new subsystem (timeouts, cancellation, retries) the reporter didn't ask
  for, isn't a sweep fix: ship the small part and 🎫 the rest. Match the
  versions the workspace already pins; a sweep is not a dependency upgrade.
- Never tune agent instructions or prompts around one report's wording.

## 4. Ship

Put every fix in one PR, and open it once every claimed Fix report has a
fix or a failed attempt, so CI waits come after the fixing. Don't open one
PR per item. End the PR body with a
`## Reports` heading listing the link of every report the PR fixes: the
Slack thread, or the Sentry, Analytics, or GitHub issue. That list is the
only set of threads a later `/ship` may close out as fixed.

Wait for CI with one command that blocks until every check finishes, and
wait on it with the longest call your tool allows, not a short call you
repeat: every call re-sends your whole context.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
Here that command is `pnpm ci:wait <number>`: it prints nothing until CI is
done, then one summary. Exit 1 means a check failed. Exit 2 means it couldn't
tell, and its last line says why: rerun a cancelled check, run the command
again when time ran out with checks still going, and otherwise look at the PR
yourself. To need fewer calls, pass `--max-minutes` about a minute
under your tool's call limit.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->
Without a repo command for it, run
`gh pr checks <number> --watch --interval 60 > /dev/null` in one call bounded
by your tool's limit, then read `gh pr checks <number>` twice, a minute
apart: CI is done only when both reads list the same checks, at least one,
and none is pending. Otherwise wait again the same way and rerun any cancelled check; after
about two hours, stop and look at the PR yourself.

Fix each review round's findings in one batch. If a second round still finds
a problem in the same fix, take that fix out of the PR, remove its whole entry
from the PR's `Reports` section: the link and its `fix-proof:` and `visual:`
lines (close-out marks every listed report fixed, and a stray evidence line
counts toward the report above it). Then 🎫 its
report with what review found, and merge the rest. Close the PR only when nothing verified
is left in it.

Merge it the way this repo merges PRs. In a Factory workspace, that means
the workflow's merge step after its merge gate, never a direct merge.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
In the framework repo, run `/ship` through the merge.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->

A sweep's PR contains product fixes only. Don't edit this skill, add checker
scripts, or add bookkeeping files in it. If the run taught something, propose
a one-line lesson in the recap for a maintainer to accept or drop.

## 5. Close the loop

This step is the only place a claimed report gets its closing reply. Run it
after the merge for the threads in the PR's `Reports` section. If the merge
happened outside this run, the next sweep runs it: when you collect, list the
sweep PRs merged in the window (`gh pr list --state merged --limit 100 --search
"merged:>=<date>"`) and close out every report in their `Reports` sections
that still lacks its ✅, however old the report is.
Entries that aren't Slack threads get no Slack action: GitHub issues follow
the issue rule below, and Sentry and Analytics issues are only listed in the
recap.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
In the framework repo, `/ship` step 6 runs this step after its merge, and
`address-feedback-with-replies` runs it for its own threads.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->
Run it once per thread: if a reply in the thread already links this PR, just make sure ✅ is
there and move on.

Write only as the connected Slack profile, only in the feedback
channels, and in the reply format from the contract above. First re-read
the contract and this step from fresh `origin/main` (`git fetch origin main
&& git show origin/main:.agents/skills/review-latest-feedback/SKILL.md`): a
run that started hours ago may be holding older rules. Re-read each thread before
writing. If a maintainer has since added `:mag:` or a person has taken it over,
leave it. If a newer human reply says it's still broken, leave the 👀 for the
next sweep. Otherwise:

- **Merged fix:** add ✅ and reply that it's fixed, with the PR linked, and
  will be on beta shortly. Only for reports whose `Reports` entry carries a
  proof (step 3). Without one, it's 🎫 and a reply that the fix is logged for a
  person to check.
- **Fix ready but not merged yet** (for example CI is still running when the
  run must end): reply that a fix (PR linked) is in review. Don't mention
  beta yet. The next run adds ✅ once it's merged, with no second reply.
- **Needs a person:** add 🎫 and say in plain words what's known and what's
  needed, without naming anyone ("thanks - logged for a product decision").
- **Couldn't reproduce:** add 🎫. If one small answer from the reporter would
  unblock it and you couldn't find it yourself, ask for just that. Otherwise
  say you couldn't reproduce it yet. Never ask
  for anything already in the thread.

GitHub issues fixed by the merged PR get a one-line thank-you comment linking
the PR, and then get closed. Post it even when someone else opened the issue,
or the PR already closed it: reporters should be told.
<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
Report unresolved CI, deploy, and chat-health failures in the private run
recap. Do not create Slack channel messages or GitHub issues for them.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->

Before ending, re-read each thread you touched and check:

- every 👀 from this run has an investigated disposition and, unless a person
  has taken over, a reply plus ✅, 🎫, or an open fix PR listed under `Reports`;
- every ✅ corresponds to a merged fix;
- no reply is technical or duplicated.

## 6. Recap

Keep the recap short, for the maintainer reading it:

```md
## Feedback sweep - <date, Pacific>
Fixed and merged (N): <one line each, with Slack thread link> · PR <link>
Closed out from earlier runs (N): <Slack thread link> · PR <link>
Needs a person (N): <what's needed, who, what you tried>
Still open from earlier runs (N): <why>
Seen, not picked (N): <Slack thread link> - <one-line reason>
Roots: <n> seen, <n> claimed, <n> left
Sources unavailable: <list or "none">
Lesson (optional): <one line>
```

"Fixed and merged" is this run's PR only; reports you closed out for an
earlier run's merged PR go under "Closed out from earlier runs".

In an automation, append the same recap to its `memory.md`.

content:
---
name: review-prs
description: >-
  Review recent BuilderIO/agent-native human pull requests, approve eligible
  internal PRs, and identify PRs ready for the user's final decision.
  Outside Factory governance, merge only when the user explicitly requests it
  for that PR. Factory governance is approval-only. Use for scheduled or manual PR
  sweeps; flag external work needing a major product call or new framework API,
  and unresolved major product or UX decisions, to a maintainer.
user-invocable: true
scope: dev
metadata:
  internal: true
---

# Review Pull Requests

Review the newest relevant human pull requests in `BuilderIO/agent-native`.
Under the default internal-author policy below, approve eligible fixes from
verified BuilderIO organization members. Never submit an approval review for an
external or unverified author; `community-prs` assigns that code-review
decision to a human Builder dev. When the user explicitly gives the manual blanket
instruction for a non-Factory review sweep defined below, follow it over
ordinary approval gates; the non-waivable safeguards still apply.

In this skill, the user is the person running a manual invocation, and a
maintainer is a verified current BuilderIO organization member who is not a
bot.

Approval and merge readiness are separate. **Ready for your final approval**
means implementation is complete, required checks have passed, and any required
product or UX decision is complete. It identifies a candidate for the user's
final decision; readiness alone does not authorize a merge. Factory governance
never performs or invokes a merge: only the
designated Factory workflow may merge a Builder PR after its merge gate. Outside
Factory governance, merge only when the user explicitly requests the merge for that
PR, using the applicable merge path below. Factory governance records a manual
disposition for confirmed external authors through its action and never
approves them. Every invocation stands down on a fork PR assigned to a
verified BuilderIO member, as required by `community-prs`. Other invocations
apply the external-contribution gate below; external authors are never eligible
for an approval review. Surface external work that needs a major product call
or a new framework API for a maintainer's explicit approval before a full review or
merge; a scheduled or manual sweep is not that approval.

## Selection and evidence

List open PRs newest by creation or update time, then inspect the latest
Agent-Native work first. Include recent PRs from internal team members even if
their branch name does not contain a product name. Re-review a PR when it has a
new commit, review, comment, or check result; otherwise do not create duplicate
review noise.

Before selecting a PR for review, read only enough metadata to determine its
author and draft state:

 - Ignore every bot-authored PR, including Dependabot and
   `builder-io-integration[bot]`, and ignore every PR authored by the active
   GitHub login (`gh api user --jq .login`). Do not inspect their diff, checks, reviews, membership,
   or source links; do not take any review or merge action; and do not add
   them to the end-of-run recap.

 - Ignore draft PRs completely. Do not inspect their diff, checks, reviews,
   membership, or source links; do not take any review action; and do not add
   them to the end-of-run recap.

 - Verify each remaining human author's current BuilderIO membership using the
   organization membership API below before applying any existing-approval
   filter. For a PR from a fork, check assignees before any other gate: if any
   assignee is a verified current BuilderIO member, ignore the PR completely,
   like a draft. That member owns it under `community-prs`. Take no review,
   reply, action, or merge action, and leave it out of the recap. This exclusion
   applies in Factory governance too.

 - For every other confirmed external PR in Factory governance, call
   `govern-factory-pull-request` so the action records a manual disposition,
   even when the PR already has a current-head approval. Do not use the manual
   external-scope or reply path for that PR, and never approve it. In other
   invocations, apply the external-contribution scope gate before reading
   review summaries or entering the evidence sweep. For PRs that continue,
   determine whether any existing current-head approval is eligible to suppress
   duplicate code review under the reviewer and newer-event rules below.

 - Reuse that review as the code assessment only after verifying the reviewer
   is a different, current BuilderIO member and is eligible under the PR's
   author- and scope-specific rules, including any independent-review
   requirement. An unknown or ineligible reviewer never suppresses a full diff
   review. A valid approval suppresses duplicate code review only while no
   newer commit, comment, review, or check result exists; the PR still enters
   the merge-readiness pass and recap.

All non-draft human PRs that pass the author and external-scope gates enter the
evidence sweep below. For PRs with a verified eligible current-head approval and
no newer event, skip duplicate code review but check merge readiness. Only a
manual, non-Factory invocation may merge, and only after the user explicitly
requests it for that PR. Eligible Liam PRs with only older-head approvals enter
the sweep so the current head can be reviewed. The blanket approval instruction
may waive ordinary approval gates, but it does not
bypass the complete diff and safety review. It need not produce a readiness
disposition or a full-sweep recap.

For every PR you inspect, read:

 - the title, body, linked issue, and source links;
 - for PRs requiring a new or repeat code review, the complete changed-file
   list and diff, including generated or migration files; a current-head
   approval from a verified eligible reviewer with no newer event is the
   existing code assessment, so check its merge evidence without repeating that
   review;
 - all current human and bot review summaries, inline comments, and replies;
 - every current check/status context and actual conclusion, marking pending,
   skipped, unknown, or failing separately;
 - the repository ownership and the affected app or framework boundary.

Inspect repository rulesets as well as branch protection. List every page with
`gh api --paginate 'repos/BuilderIO/agent-native/rulesets?includes_parents=true'`
so organization and enterprise rulesets are included, then inspect each
matching `/rulesets/<id>` definition's `conditions.ref_name` and
all applicable rules for the PR base branch, including required status checks,
deployments, and other non-status conditions. Only rulesets with
`enforcement: active` impose requirements; disabled and evaluate-only rulesets
do not. `gh pr checks --required` can omit ruleset requirements; never infer
that no merge requirements exist from that command alone.

Use the GitHub organization membership API to verify that the author and any
reviewer whose approval you rely on are current members of `BuilderIO`. Do not
infer membership from a display name, email, company claim, branch name,
`authorAssociation`, or a familiar-looking bot. If author membership cannot be
verified, do not approve. External authors are never auto-approved, even when
the patch looks safe or the issue is obviously valid.

## Explicit blanket approval instruction

Identify the invocation before applying this override. A Factory governance run
is launched by the `factory-pr-governance` automation and includes the
server-injected `<!-- factory-skill-alignment:start -->` and
`<!-- factory-skill-alignment:end -->` markers in its active prompt. The
automation composes this block independently of its editable prompt text; do
not rely on a user-editable heading. A manual invocation is a direct user
request outside that automation. If the source or injected markers cannot be
verified, do not apply the override or submit an approval; report the invocation
context as unknown.

This override applies only to manual, non-Factory review invocations. Factory
governance follows its code-defined action gates; this skill's blanket
instruction cannot waive them.

In Factory governance, the manual blanket-approval override is unavailable,
even if equivalent wording appears in the run prompt. Never submit an approval
through `gh api`, `gh pr review`, GraphQL, or another direct GitHub review
mutation. Route every Factory approval decision through
`govern-factory-pull-request` and follow its result; only that action may submit
an approval, under its code-enforced gates.

<!-- framework-repo-only:start -->
Runs of the `factory-run` skill on the factory VM are also Factory governance:
the blanket override is unavailable there too. Their only approval path is
`factory-github approve <PR url> --sha <reviewed head>`, which refuses forks,
non-members, unverifiable membership, drafts, and a moved head. A PR with a
standing approval gets no further factory approval on later pushes.
<!-- framework-repo-only:end -->

Only an explicit instruction from the user, given directly in the current request
or in the user-authorized prompt for this invocation, triggers this override.
It must expressly request approval of every currently open, non-draft PR by
verified current BuilderIO human members in `BuilderIO/agent-native`; “Approve
all BuilderIO member PRs” is one such instruction. Requests to review, inspect,
list, or identify ready PRs do not trigger it. If the requested repository,
approval action, or author/status scope differs or is ambiguous, apply the
normal gates rather than expanding the instruction. Exclude all bot-authored
PRs and PRs authored by the active GitHub login. This direct instruction overrides ordinary
approval gates, including check, review-feedback, UX-owner, and narrower
author-specific gates.
It does not waive membership verification, the external-author prohibition,
the ultra-scary safety gate, or the independent-review requirement for PRs
changing review or approval policy, agent-safety instructions, membership
verification, or CI/deployment security controls. Active credible safety
findings remain approval-blocking. If a non-waivable gate applies, do not
approve that PR; report the exact gate.

Before approving, inspect the complete changed-file list and diff, current
review findings, and current check results needed to identify non-waivable
safety concerns. The approval can serve as code-review evidence in a later
readiness pass only because this path requires that full diff review; it remains
reusable only under the reviewer eligibility, current-head, and no-newer-event
rules above. It cannot satisfy a required independent-review gate: when that
gate applies, require a separate, non-dismissed, current-head `APPROVED` review
from a verified current BuilderIO member other than the blanket approver. Do
not count or reuse the blanket approval as independent-review evidence. Do not
infer a code assessment from the blanket instruction alone.

For each eligible PR, record the head whose complete diff was reviewed. Re-read
the live head immediately before acting. If it changed during or after review,
restart the complete diff and safety review against the new head; do not approve
until that review is complete. Submit at most one approval for the reviewed
head, and do not duplicate an existing current-head approval. If membership or
the exact reviewed head cannot be verified, do not approve that PR and report
the specific verification failure. This instruction authorizes approvals only.
Do not merge from this path. Do not comment or reply unless the user separately
asks; Factory governance still never merges or invokes a merge workflow. Keep
the recap concise, but report the exact check and actionable-feedback states
for each approval even when ordinary gates are overridden. Distinguish approval
from readiness and include any verification or non-waivable safety exceptions;
omit unrelated risk inventory unless the user asks for it.

## External-contribution scope gate

Builder devs decide bounded outside contributions; maintainers keep major
product calls and new framework APIs.

For an author the membership API confirms is not a current BuilderIO member,
continue into the normal evidence sweep for a clear bug fix or a bounded
improvement. A clear bug fix corrects a specific reported or reproducible
defect by restoring intended behavior. A bounded improvement stays within one
established workflow, app, or framework area and follows the patterns already
there.

External work needs a maintainer when it makes a major product call (as defined under
Product and UX decisions) or adds a new framework API: a new public export,
configuration option, action, plugin or hook contract, or CLI surface in a
published package under `packages/`. A fix or bounded improvement to an existing
API stays with devs when it keeps that API's contract. If the title, issue, and
initial diff do not establish a clear bug fix or a bounded improvement, treat it
as needing a maintainer.

For external work that needs a maintainer, stop before the full code review, approval
or review action, merge-readiness disposition, author-facing draft, or merge.
Report it as **Needs a maintainer's approval for scope**, with the PR link,
author, stated scope, and which call it needs. Wait for a maintainer's explicit go-ahead on
that PR before continuing. Invoking or scheduling `review-prs`, approving a
different PR, or prior approval of another external contribution does not
authorize it. If membership is unknown, use the existing unknown-membership
policy; do not classify the author as external. The scope gate does not apply
solely because membership could not be verified. Keep the no-approval outcome,
report the missing membership check, and assess merge readiness under the
existing unknown-membership policy.

Builder devs own outside PRs end to end with `community-prs`.

## Liamdebeasi approval policy

For a PR authored by the exact GitHub login `liamdebeasi` and immutable user
ID `2721089`, always submit an approval when it is a current, non-draft PR in
`BuilderIO/agent-native`, the membership API verifies current BuilderIO
membership, and it does not already have a current-head, non-dismissed
approval; never duplicate an existing approval. This exception overrides the
ordinary check, ordinary review-feedback, scope, and UX-owner gates. It does
not override membership verification, the ultra-scary safety gate, or the
independent-review requirement for PRs changing review or approval policy,
agent-safety instructions, membership verification, or CI/deployment security
controls. Active credible safety findings remain approval-blocking. It does
not authorize a merge.

## Internal-author approval policy

The user has explicitly authorized a practical internal-author exception for
this skill:

 - For a verified current BuilderIO member, failed, pending, skipped, or
   unknown CI/check evidence does not by itself block approval. Record the
   exact state in the recap and assume the author will resolve it before merge.
 - For a verified current BuilderIO member, ordinary unresolved review
   feedback, including bot findings, does not by itself block approval. Record
   the unresolved feedback and assume it will be handled before merge.
 - These exceptions do not waive the ultra-scary safety gate below. Do not
   approve when the current diff or review evidence indicates a credible auth
   bypass, permission or tenant-isolation failure, secret or credential leak,
   destructive data loss or migration, remote code execution, SSRF, payment
   compromise, deployment compromise, or similarly severe production risk.
 - Do not claim that ignored checks are green or that ignored feedback is
   resolved. The recap must distinguish approval under the internal exception
   from a clean merge state.

When an exception requires independent review, it means a separate,
attributable, non-dismissed `APPROVED` PR review from a different verified
current BuilderIO member, submitted against the current PR head and remaining
that reviewer’s latest non-dismissed review, with no active, non-dismissed
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` review from any reviewer.
Self-review, author-stated validation, bot-only review, a
`COMMENTED`/`CHANGES_REQUESTED` review, an unverified reviewer, or
unverifiable review state does not satisfy it; without that evidence, do not
use the exception.

## Owner exceptions

The verified owner exceptions are:

 - Nick (`NKoech123`) - Slides
 - Shomix (`shomix`, GitHub user ID `100691266`) - any app or framework area
 - Enzo (`enzoames`) - Factory, only when the PR is specific to the Factory
   app

For a verified PR authored by Alice and limited to Content app or template
behavior, including supporting shared framework or Desktop plumbing required
by that Content feature, or authored by Nick and limited to Slides app
behavior, including supporting shared framework plumbing, auto-approve by

checks, and ordinary unresolved human or bot feedback. These owner exceptions
override the normal UX-owner, narrow-refactor, check, and review-resolution

Treat a PR as Factory-specific only when the changed behavior is limited to

Shared framework changes that materially affect other apps, Slack ingestion,

For a verified PR authored by Shomix (`shomix`, GitHub user ID `100691266`),

For a verified PR authored by Sid, or by Enzo (`enzoames`) when the PR is

For a verified PR authored by `kapunahelewong` or Wes (`bwreid`), auto-approve

or other production-code change. This docs exception also overrides the
normal UX-owner, narrow-refactor, check, and review-resolution gates.

All owner and docs exceptions still require current BuilderIO membership and
do not waive the ultra-scary safety gate or the external-author prohibition.
A PR involving preview execution, credential routing, tenant isolation,

## Standard approval gate

This is the default gate; the explicit blanket approval instruction above takes
precedence when invoked.

For verified internal authors who do not qualify for a verified owner or docs
exception, approve only when all of the following are true after applying the
internal-author policy:

1. The PR is in `BuilderIO/agent-native` and the author is a verified current
   BuilderIO organization member.
2. It fixes a clear, repo-owned issue with a narrow root-cause change. The
   evidence supports the changed boundary, and the PR does not encode one
   chat report as a brittle global prompt or situation-specific rule.
3. There is no ultra-scary concern involving security, auth, permissions,
   secrets, data loss, destructive migrations, remote code execution, SSRF,
   payments, deployment safety, or an unexplained dependency/infrastructure
   change.
4. The scope and affected behavior are understood. Escalate unresolved major
   product or UX decisions as described below. Owner exceptions govern whether
   to submit an approval review; they do not create an additional owner-approval
   requirement for code readiness.

Do not approve external authors, unverified authors, or internal PRs whose
remaining concern is ultra-scary. A clean-looking diff is not enough when the
owner, runtime behavior, or release state is uncertain.

## Product and UX decisions

Assess product and UX impact from the actual diff, not just filenames. This
includes visible copy, layout, navigation, controls, settings, interaction,
loading states, accessibility behavior, and user-facing defaults. A major
decision changes a core workflow, navigation or information architecture,
product defaults or permissions, or behavior across apps. If that decision is
not already settled by a maintainer's written direction, classify it as **Needs a
maintainer's product/UX decision** and do not enter the manual merge path until
a maintainer decides.
A routine bug fix or bounded improvement within an established workflow is not
a major decision.

Keep the PR thread silent while a required product or UX decision is
unresolved. Do not comment or reply to request, announce, or explain that the
decision is needed; record the gate only in the recap. This remains true after
an author update, so do not send a thanks-only or status-only reply while the
decision is pending.

The app-owner map is for approval exceptions only; an owner approval is not a
separate code-readiness requirement:

 - Alice (`3mdistal`) - Content
 - Shomix (`shomix`) - Clips
 - Nick (`NKoech123`) - Slides
 - Nicholas - Analytics
 - Enzo (`enzoames`) - Factory
 - Sid (`sidmohanty11`) - Design

Verify the author's GitHub identity and affected app before applying an owner
exception. An app owner's status does not waive the ultra-scary safety gate or
the major product/UX decision above.

## Review actions

Factory governance submits approvals only through
`govern-factory-pull-request`, which claims and reconciles the decision and
revalidates evidence. Never call GitHub write endpoints directly from Factory
governance. If the invocation context is unknown, do not submit an approval.

The following approval procedure is for manual, non-Factory invocations only;
Factory governance must not use or adapt it. If a PR passes the applicable gate
and lacks a current-head approval, submit one GitHub approval review pinned to
the exact SHA whose complete diff you reviewed, and record the approval URL in
the recap. The review creation request must set `event=APPROVE` and
`commit_id=$reviewed_head_sha`; do not omit the reviewed SHA or use a flow that
defaults to the latest head.

Read the response and require its `commit_id` to equal
`$reviewed_head_sha`. If the request fails, the returned SHA differs, or the
live head moved after review, do not count that review as current-head evidence;
review the new head completely before retrying with its SHA. Do not duplicate
an existing current-head approval. This skill reviews other people's PRs: do
not add a tag, assignment, mention, or explanatory comment unless the current
invocation explicitly authorizes that communication on the exact PR. This does
not add a separate authorization step for replies required on the active
user's own PR under `/ship`, `/ship-now`, or `/babysit-pr`.

When a PR needs product, UX, or app-owner review, record that gate only in the
recap and leave the PR thread alone. Do not comment or reply to ask for, announce,
or explain that owner review is needed. This silence rule applies even after an
author update; do not send a thanks-only or status reply while that review gate is
outstanding.
This silence rule does not suppress replies required on the active user's own PR
under `/ship`, `/ship-now`, or `/babysit-pr`; those follow the own-PR reply rules.

When a reply is needed to resolve a review thread on the exact PR the current
invocation authorizes, only a verified external author gets one. Confirm the author
is a nonmember first. An unknown-membership author gets no reply, and the membership
check goes in the recap. Verified BuilderIO members get no reply here. The active
user's own PR is the one exception: it gets the disposition only, with no thank-you.
For a verified external author, an explicit reply request sends the reply even
without an author update. Otherwise reply only if the author has updated since the
last message, and begin by thanking them for the PR or for their update. An explicit
request does not override the owner-review silence rule above, except on the active
user's own PR. Never write “I have no further feedback” or another vague closing;
state the disposition and the next actor and action, such as the exact change
requested, that no changes are requested and the PR is ready for maintainer
merge, or which named check is still pending. If the next step is a product,
UX, or app-owner decision, use the silence rule above.

Bot-authored PRs, including Dependabot, are outside this skill's review and
merge scope and must remain completely untouched.

For a PR that fails an ordinary approval gate overridden by the explicit
blanket instruction, the approval may proceed only after the full diff and
safety review above. A non-waivable gate always blocks approval, even under the
blanket instruction; if one applies, do not submit an approval and flag the
exact concern and evidence needed to resolve it. External or unverified authors
never receive an approval review. Outside Factory governance, their PRs may
still be assessed for code readiness, but merging requires the user's explicit
request for that PR and all readiness gates below. Confirmed external PRs must
also pass the external-contribution scope gate; external work that needs a
major product call or a new framework API remains stopped at the maintainer approval
gate. For unknown membership, do not apply the external scope gate solely
because verification failed; preserve the no-approval outcome, assess readiness
under the existing unknown-membership policy, and name the missing check.

## Merge-ready disposition and handoff

For every human PR in the evidence sweep, assess readiness regardless of whether
this skill can submit an approval. Use the BuilderIO membership API; a confirmed
nonmember is external, while lookup or visibility failures leave membership
unknown. Only prepare author-facing reply drafts for authors verified as
external. Never draft a reply for a verified BuilderIO member, including a
thank-you; report requested updates in the recap instead. If membership is
unknown, do not treat the author as external or draft a reply.

Classify the PR as **Ready for your final approval**,
**Needs updates**, **Needs a maintainer's product/UX decision**, or **Cannot assess**.
Ready means the current head is sound, implementation is complete, every
required check and status context has passed, any required independent review
above is present on the current head, any required product or UX decision is
complete, and actionable human or automated findings have a verified fix or
evidence-backed terminal disposition. The user retains the final decision. PRs
still waiting on a required check, independent review, or product/UX decision
are not ready.
An active human `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review or unresolved actionable request
blocks readiness; resolved, superseded, or non-actionable threads do not.
Missing approval or `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED` alone does not make the
code **Needs updates**; it remains a pending human merge requirement and must be
reported separately from code readiness. Conflicts, pending or failed required
checks, active actionable bot findings, credible safety concerns, or a material
code issue mean **Needs updates** or **Cannot assess**. Report skipped, unknown,
and non-required checks accurately; never describe them as passing.

Independent-review requirements above govern approval actions, reuse of
existing approvals, code readiness, and merge. When they apply, the required
separate approval from a verified current BuilderIO member must be present on
the current head before the PR is ready or can merge. The user's direct merge
request and a GitHub admin bypass do not replace that evidence. Factory
governance must follow its own merge gate and never use this skill's admin or
queue commands. If no eligible current-head approval supplies the existing
code assessment, inspect the complete diff and decide readiness from that
evidence.

A ready disposition is a private handoff for the user's final decision, not an
instruction to merge. Do not merge based on readiness alone. The merge gate
and commands below apply only to manual, non-Factory execution after the user
explicitly requests a merge for that PR. In Factory governance, stop before
this section's merge actions, report the current disposition, and leave merging
to the Factory workflow.
Once all the conditions hold, record the live `headRefOid`; they must remain
true for 10 consecutive minutes on that same head:

 - every status context required by branch protection or an applicable
   repository ruleset is satisfied on the recorded head according to GitHub's
   merge rules. Record the actual conclusion; count `neutral` or `skipped` only
   when GitHub treats that result as satisfied. Pending, failed, and unknown
   contexts are not satisfied. Every other applicable merge requirement (such
   as a required deployment) must also be satisfied;
 - every actionable review finding has a verified fix or terminal disposition;
 - the PR is `MERGEABLE` with no conflicts;
 - the same recorded `headRefOid` remains unchanged for the entire 10-minute
   interval, and all checks and review dispositions apply to that head.

Reset the 10-minute gate after a push, failed check, new actionable feedback,
new commit, or merge conflict. Do not treat this skill or a ready disposition
as standing merge authorization. For an external or membership-unknown author,
never submit an approval review through this skill. The “Ready for maintainer
review” path in `community-prs` describes a human Builder dev's approval; it does not
authorize the agent to submit that approval. Follow its ordinary merge
requirements and leave the PR unmerged until a human has approved the reviewed
head and all required checks pass. Never use `--admin` for those PRs. For
verified internal-member PRs only, GitHub's `--admin` merge is a
broad protection bypass, not one scoped to human approval. Use it only after
verifying that any required independent review above is already satisfied and
that missing human approval or
`REVIEW_REQUIRED` is the sole unsatisfied requirement, all other applicable
protections are satisfied, and no merge queue is required. Revalidate the
exact live head and all requirements immediately before invoking it. If any
non-review requirement is pending, failed, unknown, or unsatisfied, do not use
`--admin`; wait for that requirement. When no queue is required and the gate
holds, use the guarded admin merge:

This revalidation is client-side, not atomic with GitHub's admin merge.
`--match-head-commit` protects the PR head SHA but does not pin status
conclusions or ruleset configuration. Re-read active protections and required
contexts for the exact head in one final pass, then invoke the merge immediately.
If that evidence changes or cannot be read, stop and restart the gate. This
leaves a narrow time-of-check/time-of-use window inherent in the admin merge
API; it never authorizes merging with a known failed, pending, or unknown
non-review requirement.

```bash
gh pr merge <number> --repo BuilderIO/agent-native --squash --admin \
  --match-head-commit <verified-head-oid>
```

If an applicable ruleset requires a merge queue, do not use `--admin`. After
the same readiness gate holds, enqueue the exact head through GitHub's queue:

```bash
gh pr merge <number> --repo BuilderIO/agent-native --auto --squash \
  --match-head-commit <verified-head-oid>
```

Verify the queue entry's PR head against the recorded head with
`pullRequest { id headRefOid mergeQueueEntry { state position pullRequest { headRefOid } headCommit { oid } } }`.
Keep `mergeQueueEntry.pullRequest.headRefOid` equal to the recorded PR head;
track `mergeQueueEntry.headCommit.oid` separately as the merge-group candidate
used for queue checks. `--match-head-commit` only gates the enqueue request; it
does not pin a later auto-merge or queue entry to that SHA.

Whenever a gate reset occurs after a queue entry or auto-merge request is
active, immediately dequeue any active queue entry and disable any active
auto-merge request, then verify both `mergeQueueEntry` and `autoMergeRequest`
are absent. This applies to every reset cause, including a head change, failed
check, new actionable feedback, new commit, or merge conflict. Re-review the
changed head or feedback and enqueue again only after the full 10-minute gate
passes. Never leave a stale readiness decision queued to merge.

```bash
gh api graphql -F id='<pull-request-node-id>' -f query='mutation($id: ID!) { dequeuePullRequest(input: { id: $id }) { mergeQueueEntry { state } } }'
gh pr merge <number> --repo BuilderIO/agent-native --disable-auto
```

Use the dequeue mutation only when a queue entry exists and `--disable-auto`
only when auto-merge is enabled. Do not report the PR merged until its state is
`MERGED`, then verify the merge commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`. If the
queue cannot proceed solely because a human approval is required, report that
queue/approval policy conflict to the user; do not send the PR to another reviewer
or bypass the queue.

For a verified BuilderIO-member PR outside Factory governance, when the user
explicitly asks to merge,
`REVIEW_REQUIRED` alone is not a reason to wait for another reviewer; use the
guarded admin merge only if all conditions above hold. After the command,
re-query the PR for its merged state and merge commit, fetch
`origin/main`, and verify that commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`. Report a
merge only after that verification; otherwise report the actual pending or
not-merged state. If the head or another gate changes, restart the gate. Merge
only if the user explicitly requested it for this PR and no code or author action
is needed; otherwise report its private readiness disposition.

For every verified external PR needing a code update or evidence necessary to
assess a material behavior change, draft a concise reply that names the concrete
change or evidence requested and links the relevant review thread or check when
useful. Before drafting, inspect
the PR timeline, commits, and review threads for all actionable requests from
maintainers. If any request remains unaddressed, do not draft or
post another author-facing comment. In particular, if the latest PR activity is
a maintainer asking for an update and no later contributor reply or relevant commit
addresses it, mark the PR as waiting and do not add another comment. A
contributor commit or substantive reply clears only the requests it actually
addresses; an unrelated commit or bare acknowledgment does not. Mark the PR as
waiting on the contributor and link each outstanding request. Once all prior
requests are addressed, reassess the current head and draft only the remaining
code or screenshot requests. This also applies when another comment or bot
event is newer than the maintainer's request; bot activity alone does not reopen the
handoff.

On a contributor-owned PR, do not draft a follow-up unless the author has made
